 Watch: Sammy Kershaw and Rodney Atkins walk CMA Awards red carpet after controversy
 The Tennessean Follow Peter Burditt, Nashville Tennessean Add to Preferred Sources Updated Thu, November 19, 2026 at 12:20 AM UTC Sammy Kershaw and Rodney Atkins have walked across the red carpet after publicly criticizing the CMA for denying their separate requests to walk the red carpet, sparking a controversy that became one of the biggest talking points of this year's CMA Awards.
 "I didn't mean to hurt anybody, but it went where it needed to go," Kershaw told The Tennessean on the red carpet. "The CMAs has been good to us ever since this happened."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Kershaw and Atkins appeared after two weeks of conversation among country music fans and industry observers, a large majority of which criticized the CMA 's move given their longstanding career and contributions to the genre.
 Sammy Kershaw and Mendy Kershaw arrive on the red carpet at the 60th Annual CMA Awards at Bridgestone Arena in Nashville, Tenn., Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026. Following the backlash, the CMA released an official statement and invited the veteran singers to walk the red carpet and attend the event. Days after the CMA's statement, the controversy was put to bed after Kershaw and Atkins accepted their invitations.
 "I don't want to forget about the people who brought me here," Kershaw added, explaining why he chose to speak out about being denied red carpet access.
 What did Sammy Kershaw and Rodney Atkins say about their CMA red carpet snub?
 "Well, I just found out some disappointing news and it really hurts me," Kershaw wrote at the beginning of his Facebook post on Nov. 5.
 Advertisement Advertisement "I have to share my disappointment with the CMA as they have denied my request to walk the red carpet for a few minutes at this year's CMA Awards, and I have to say I'm pretty sad about it."
 Kershaw also said he had been "strung along for several months" before the CMA informed him that his request to walk the carpet had been denied.
 Atkins said days later that he, too, had been denied access to the CMA Awards.
 How did the CMA respond to the controversy?
 After days of protest and pushback, the CMA released a statement on Nov. 9 saying that the red carpet "has criteria that exists to help manage limited space and the security needs for both the artists and the media."
 Advertisement Advertisement "We are deeply sorry anyone felt excluded by those decisions...Our organization's mission is to honor the history and celebrate the excellence of Country Music. With this 60th anniversary year, we are working extra hard to simultaneously spotlight the last six decades, while also celebrating what has been a tremendous year in 2026. It's not easy to do all of that in just one night, but we are up for the challenge."
 More to explore
 "We also know this is about more than a red carpet, and we are committed to keep listening and keep finding ways to make sure all artists feel welcome and at home here. To that point, we are in touch with Sammy Kershaw's team and look forward to continuing that conversation," the statement concluded.
 Kershaw posted again after the CMA's statement, saying that the controversy extended beyond his own experience and that the CMA's statement "fell short of addressing the heart of the issue."
 Sammy Kershaw and Rodney Atkins accept CMA's invitation
 Kershaw and Atkins confirmed that they would be walking the CMA red carpet days after the statement was released, putting the roughly two-week saga to an end.
 Advertisement Advertisement "After a lot of thought and prayer, Mendy and I have decided to accept the CMAs invitation to walk the red carpet and attend the awards," Kershaw wrote in his post .
 "To the thousands of fans and fellow artists who stood beside us, please know that you helped make this happen," the '90s country star concluded.
 In his post , Atkins said he would also be walking the red carpet and attending the awards show.
 "After some good conversations between our team and the CMA, Rose and I have decided we'll be walking the red carpet and attending this year's awards."
 "I'm grateful to the CMA for hearing us out, and I can't thank y'all enough for all the love and support...Now I've just gotta find a red-carpet-worthy ball cap," Atkins added.
